column1: # Mica's own hardening requirements (the parsing-family hardening work of

column3: Duplicate-attribute checks are linear in the attributes of an element
Prefix resolution is linear in declarations and names
ATTLIST defaults apply in time linear in declarations and elements
Character references expand in linear time (CVE-2024-49761 shape)
Entity expansion is linear in the output (CVE-2024-41946 shape)
Long names, many siblings and deep nesting parse in linear time
Content models, enumerations and declarations parse in linear time
Streamed input moves each byte O(1) times
Buffer compaction in Core::ByteInput is linear
Line and column queries are amortized O(1)
Substring search is linear (KMP)
Descendant chains never revisit subtrees
Axis steps from many contexts are linear
Node-set comparisons and string functions are linear
Many '<' in attribute values parse in linear time
Terminator lookalikes in comments, PIs and CDATA parse in linear time
Runs of ']', '>]' and white space parse in linear time
Deep elements with same-local-name attributes parse in linear time
Ordinary documents parse well inside the default budget
Budget overruns raise WorkBudgetExceededError with position, operations and allowance
A wall-clock deadline is enforced during scanning and at every stream refill
Long-lived streams renew the meter between messages
XPath evaluation runs under a budget and deadline positioned in the expression
WorkBudget allowances saturate; WorkMeter verdicts
Every hostile byte class in every context ends in acceptance or a Mica::Error, with exact positions
Every proper prefix of a document is rejected identically from bytes and streams
Seeded mutation fuzzing finds no crash, overrun or nondeterminism
Billion-laughs and quadratic-blowup inputs stop quickly
Depth, attribute, name, token, input and default-attribute limits
External DTDs and entities are never read
Name hashing is seeded per table
Errors carry line, column (in characters) and byte offset
A String and a trickling IO produce the same events
Parse, serialize and parse again gives the same tree
Strict UTF-8 decoding accepts exactly the canonical encodings
Byte order marks, labels and transcoding without iconv
A binary format runs on Core::ByteInput with no core changes
Core enforces token, input-size and work limits for any format
The complexity harness flags superlinear growth
The fuzz harness is replayable and classifies crashes, overruns and nondeterminism
The traceability helper reports covered, uncovered and unknown ids
